result:
Solution 1 is the only one whose answer, 2n − 2, holds up. I read pd as the projective dimension of S/𝒫(J_𝒞), and I did not check Solution 1's upper-bound argument beyond the n = 2 case.

**Upper bound.** By Hochster's formula, pd(S/I) = 2n − 1 would require H̃₀(Δ) ≠ 0 for the full vertex set. So the Stanley–Reisner complex Δ would have to be disconnected.

For a nonempty code, no generator contains both x_i and y_i, so {x_i, y_i} is always an edge of Δ. For Δ to be disconnected, some pair of blocks i, j would need no edges between them. That requires x_ix_j, x_iy_j, y_ix_j and y_iy_j all to be generators, which would exclude every codeword. So Δ is connected, and pd ≤ 2n − 2.

**Achievability.** Take 𝒞 = {0ⁿ, 1ⁿ}. Then 𝒫(J_𝒞) = (x_iy_j : i ≠ j). Its complex has facets {x₁,…,x_n}, {y₁,…,y_n} and {x_i, y_i}. Mayer–Vietoris gives H̃₁(Δ) ≅ k^{n−1} ≠ 0 for n ≥ 2, so pd(S/I) = 2n − 2. For n = 2 this is (x₁y₂, x₂y₁), which has pd 2, matching 2n − 2.

**Solution 2** uses the empty code. Its canonical form is {1}, not {x_i, 1 − x_i}, so the polarized ideal is the unit ideal and the claimed maximum of 2n − 1 is wrong.

**Solution 3** claims a maximum of n. Its own example {00, 11} has pd 2 = n only because n = 2, and the case 𝒞 = {0ⁿ, 1ⁿ} with n = 3 already has pd 4 > 3.

CHOICE: 1
